Because I wanted to display the Git branch in the prompt, I changed `PS1` (The primary prompt string) in `~/.bashrc` based on [Customize the prompt to display the git branch](https://qiita.com/caad1229/items/6d71d84933c8a87af0c4), so this is a memorandum.

<script src="https://gist.github.com/atsukoba/369f8afa9bde30ceafce2d4f3b087a2c.js"></script>

After setting the above,

![my prompt](/images/ps1/1aa55461979ca2a5e392e0bf6be39425-resized.webp)

It became like this.

---

## Memorandum

According to [2.5. Bash Prompt Escape Sequences](http://tldp.org/HOWTO/Bash-Prompt-HOWTO/bash-prompt-escape-sequences.html), it is as follows.

- `\h` => Hostname
- `\u` => Username
- `\w` => Directory (full path)
- `\W` => Directory
- `\t` => Time (24-hour format)
- `\T` => Time (12-hour format)
- `\@` => AM / PM
- `\d` => Date
- `\D` => Date and time
- `\#` => Command number
- `\!` => History number
- `\n` => Newline

As for the display,

```bash
[<Command number>(<History number>)] <Time HH:MM:SS> <user> at <directory> [<branch>]
```

It becomes like this.

In the `<branch>` part, `parse_git_branch` is called, and inside it, the result of `git branch --no-color` is replaced with `sed`, and errors (`2`) are discarded to [`/dev/null`](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Null_device).

Also, as mentioned in the article above, the following variables can be used for color settings:

```shellscript
local  BLUE="\[\e[1;34m\]"
local  RED="\[\e[1;31m\]"
local  GREEN="\[\e[1;32m\]"
local  WHITE="\[\e[00m\]"
local  GRAY="\[\e[1;37m\]"
```

---

### By the way

It seems that `PS2` (The secondary prompt string) can also be set, but it's troublesome so I'll leave it alone.
